objective: Validate whether a low-privilege ThingsBoard device HTTP client can trigger memory exhaustion through chunked JSON telemetry bodies when Content-Length is absent.

static_candidate_summary.title: HTTP transport JSON body size guard can be bypassed statically when Content-Length is unknown
static_candidate_summary.source: Device HTTP transport POST bodies under /api/v1/{deviceToken}/telemetry and /api/v1/{deviceToken}/attributes.
static_candidate_summary.sink: Spring @RequestBody String followed by JsonParser.parseString and JsonConverter conversion in DeviceApiController.
static_candidate_summary.driver: Body byte volume and JSON key/value count, using Transfer-Encoding: chunked with no Content-Length.
static_candidate_summary.expected_growth: Request body String and JSON parser/converter structures grow before rejection when no Content-Length is available.

deployment_plan.model: official Docker image with PostgreSQL companion service
notes: The repository Docker quickstart defaults TB_VERSION=latest and DATABASE=postgres.
The pulled tb-node image reported ThingsBoard v4.3.1.3 at startup.
The target JVM was capped at -Xmx384m and the container at 768m for controlled validation.

data_preparation_plan: Use default sysadmin credentials only to create disposable tenant data.
Create a tenant administrator through the documented REST API and activation link flow.
Create one device with a fixed ACCESS_TOKEN credential.
Use only the device access token for the telemetry probe.

probe_plan.transport: HTTP/1.1 with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and no Content-Length
probe_plan.body_shape: JSON object with many unique telemetry keys
probe_plan.stop_condition: Stop on OOM, sustained HTTP unavailability, timeout, or safety cap.

execution_summary.reason: The 32 MiB chunked telemetry request triggered Java heap OutOfMemoryError and subsequent /login availability checks timed out.
